 Tech Taiwan conducts observation flight to improve Typhoon Champi forecasts
 Jet drops weather instruments from 13,000 meters to collect atmospheric data
   Oct. 22, 2026 15:35
 Jet crew air-dropped sensor to track Typhoon Champi. (CWA photo)
 502 TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The Central Weather Administration said Thursday that it had completed an observation flight to gather data on Typhoon Champi earlier that morning, according to a press release .
 The CWA partnered with National Taiwan University and the Aerospace Industrial Development Corporation for the mission. An Astra jet departed Taichung’s Ching Chuan Kang Airport at 5 a.m. for a flight lasting about five hours.
 The aircraft flew at an altitude of about 13,000 meters and deployed weather instruments called dropsondes around the typhoon and along its potential path. The instruments collected atmospheric temperature, pressure, humidity, wind direction, and wind speed data as they descended toward the sea.
 The data were transmitted by satellite to the CWA to help forecasters analyze Champi’s structure and development. They were also fed into numerical forecasting models to improve predictions.
 The CWA said observations over the ocean were relatively sparse, while forecasting models differed in their projections of Champi’s path and circulation. The flight gathered data from key areas to help address those gaps.
 Taiwan has completed 92 observation flights under the program since 2003, improving typhoon monitoring and forecast accuracy, the CWA said. It also shared the Champi observations with weather agencies worldwide.
